annotation.title_clean: Ethical Challenges in the Human-Robot Interaction Field
annotation.title_en: Ethical Challenges in the Human-Robot Interaction Field
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Rosén, J.; Lindblom, J.; Billing, E.; Lamb, M.
annotation.venue: HRI '21 (ACM/IEEE International Conference on Human-Robot Interaction), extended abstract; arXiv
named_instruments_referenced: APA Ethical Principles of Psychologists and Code of Conduct
EU Ethics in Social Science and Humanities guidance
annotation.summary_en: Extended abstract identifying five ethical issues in human-robot interaction research: emotion emulation, presentation of social robots, anthropomorphic terminology, data privacy, and Wizard of Oz setups. It calls for ethical board approval, informed consent, debriefing, and transparency about robot capabilities.
key_provisions_or_claims: Emulating emotions in robots may constitute deception and psychological harm requiring informed consent and debriefing
Anthropomorphic terminology (e.g., 'care robots') can create unrealistic expectations
Social robot sensors can unintentionally collect sensitive household data
No standardized ethical practice exists for Wizard of Oz studies
HRI researchers should be transparent about robot capabilities and seek ethical board approval
